observables.derivation:
The generalised eigenproblem is K*v=lambda*M*v, with K=k*[[2,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,2]] in N/m and M=m*I in kg. Thus lambda has dimension s^(-2), and omega has dimension rad/s. For z=lambda*m/k, the characteristic polynomial is (2-z)*((2-z)^2-2). Its smallest root is 2-sqrt(2).
The rational inequalities 1.4142135623730950<sqrt(2)<1.4142135623730951 follow by squaring their endpoints and suffice to round the squared frequencies and middle shape components to twelve significant digits.
observables.description: lowest squared angular frequency
observables.name: omega1_squared

observables.derivation: The central root of (2-z)*((2-z)^2-2) is z=2. With k/m=1 s^(-2), the eigenvalue is 2 s^(-2).
observables.description: middle squared angular frequency
observables.name: omega2_squared
observables.second_route: Direct multiplication gives K*[1,0,-1]^T=2*[1,0,-1]^T N/m, while M is the identity in kg.

observables.derivation: The largest root of the displayed characteristic polynomial is 2+sqrt(2). The stated rational bracket for sqrt(2) gives the recorded decimal.
observables.description: highest squared angular frequency

observables.derivation: Take the positive square root of the lowest eigenvalue. Squaring rational endpoints, together with the bracket for sqrt(2), gives 0.7653668647301795<omega1<0.7653668647301796 in rad/s.

observables.name: omega1

observables.derivation: The positive square root of 2 s^(-2) is sqrt(2) rad/s. The bracket obtained by rational squaring fixes the twelve-digit rounding.

observables.derivation: The positive square root of the highest eigenvalue lies between 1.8477590650225734 and 1.8477590650225736 rad/s, as checked by squaring and using the bracket for sqrt(2).

variants.description: cyclic coupling with one rigid-body mode and a repeated eigenvalue
variants.expected:
The stiffness is k*[[2,-1,-1],[-1,2,-1],[-1,-1,2]]=k*(3*I-J), where J is the all-ones matrix; the mass matrix remains m*I. The exact squared angular frequencies are 0,3*k/m,3*k/m, hence 0,3,3 s^(-2). The frequencies are 0 and sqrt(3) twice, with sqrt(3)=1.73205080757 rad/s to twelve significant digits.
A rigid-body shape is [1,1,1]. An orthogonal basis for the repeated eigenspace is [1,-1,0] and [1,1,-2]. The repeated eigenspace is exactly the plane v1+v2+v3=0, with orthogonal projector I-J/3. Correct spectral evidence identifies this invariant subspace; individual basis vectors inside it are not uniquely determined. On that plane J*v=0, so direct multiplication independently gives K*v=3*k*v.

observables.second_route: Substitute x=a*cos(t)+b*sin(t), with time in seconds. Coefficient matching gives 9*a+12*b=15 and -12*a+9*b=0, hence a=3/5 m and b=4/5 m. Their Euclidean amplitude is sqrt(9/25+16/25)=1 m.

observables.derivation: Both stiffness components are positive, so the phase is atan((c*omega)/(k-m*omega^2))=atan(4/3)=2*atan(1/2). The alternating series for atan(1/2), through j=22 in sum((-1)^j*(1/2)^(2*j+1)/(2*j+1)), has a next-term bound below 2e-16 after multiplication by two. It gives 0.927295218001612... rad and the stated rounding.

observables.derivation:
The particular displacement is (3/5)*cos(t)+(4/5)*sin(t) m, with t expressed in seconds. The homogeneous displacement is exp(-3*t/2)*(C*cos(t)+D*sin(t)). Zero initial displacement gives C=-3/5 m; zero initial velocity gives D=-17/10 m. This yields the displayed closed form.
At one second, cos(1)=0.5403023058681397..., sin(1)=0.8414709848078965... and exp(-3/2)=0.2231301601484298.... The particular term is 0.9973581713672010... m and the subtracted transient term is 0.3915224885429073... m. Their difference is 0.6058356828242937... m. These evaluations can be reproduced with the alternating sine and cosine series through j=9 and the exponential series through degree 30; their remainder bounds are smaller than the rounding margin for twelve significant digits.

problem.instance: A 4 kg mass is attached to a spring of stiffness 13 N/m and a damper of coefficient 12 N*s/m. A 15 N cosine force with angular frequency 1 rad/s starts at time zero. The transient displacement is requested at t=1 s.
problem.model: The displacement satisfies m*x''+c*x'+k*x=F*cos(omega*t). The spring and viscous damper are linear, the drive is prescribed, and the initial displacement and velocity vanish. Phase lag is measured relative to the cosine drive and lies between zero and pi for positive damping.

variants.description: raise damping to separate the fast and slow homogeneous timescales
variants.expected:
The characteristic roots are r_plus=(-100+sqrt(9987))/2 and r_minus=(-100-sqrt(9987))/2 in s^(-1). Both are negative. The ratio of their magnitudes is (100+sqrt(9987))/(100-sqrt(9987)), strictly between 3000 and 3100. This separates the initial fast decay from the slow relaxation and stresses time-stepping stiffness.
The steady amplitude is 15/sqrt(160081) m and the phase lag is atan(400/9). Writing a=135/160081 m and b=6000/160081 m, the exact displacement is a*cos(t)+b*sin(t)+((r_minus*a-b/(1 s))/(r_plus-r_minus))*exp(r_plus*t)+((b/(1 s)-r_plus*a)/(r_plus-r_minus))*exp(r_minus*t), with the trigonometric argument t/(1 s). The coefficients enforce zero initial displacement and velocity.
A stepping comparison records discretisation error against this closed form separately from representation, arithmetic and verification contributions. A small arithmetic radius alone does not certify a trajectory's discretisation error.
variants.name: overdamped

observables.derivation:
The steady continuum solution is T(x)=T_left+(T_right-T_left)*x/L. At the first node this gives 273.15+100/4=298.15 K. The discrete system is A*T=[T_left,0,T_right]^T, with A=[[2,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,2]] dimensionless and both sides in K. Multiplying by conductivity/h^2 restores the physical conduction operator, whose dimension is W/(m^3*K), and an equation residual in W/m^3.
A second difference of a linear profile vanishes exactly. Consequently these nodal values have no spatial discretisation error for this specific steady model.

problem.instance: The rod occupies 0<=x<=1 m. Its ends are at 273.15 K and 373.15 K. Interior nodes are at 1/4,1/2,3/4 m. For the transient variant, the open rod interior is initially uniform at 273.15 K; the boundary values are imposed for positive time, so the initial right-end mismatch is intentional.
problem.model:
A uniform rod has constant conductivity and diffusivity, no internal heat generation and fixed end temperatures. Steady conduction satisfies T''=0. The transient model is T_t=alpha*T_xx. A central second difference uses three interior points with spacing h=L/4. Temperature coordinates are converted to kelvin before assembly.
The temperature-scale selector chooses either the kelvin endpoint parameters or their Celsius alternatives. Celsius parameters are alternative coordinates of the same boundary temperatures, not additional uncertain physical inputs. The time-regime selector chooses steady or transient use.

variants.description: pose the same boundary temperatures as affine Celsius coordinates
variants.expected:
The Celsius endpoint values 0 and 100 map to 273.15 K and 373.15 K by adding the exact offset 273.15 K. The Celsius interior coordinates are exactly 25,50,75; the corresponding kelvin temperatures are 298.15,323.15,348.15.
Every temperature difference is unchanged: each grid increment is 25 K and the total endpoint difference is 100 K. Absolute coordinate numbers shift by 273.15. Assembly operates on canonical kelvin temperatures; multiplying an absolute Celsius coordinate as though it were a multiplicative unit is not the conversion rule. Decimal-to-binary conversion accounting remains distinct from the exact affine mathematical conversion.

variants.description: decay from the stated uniform interior temperature
variants.expected:
For 0<x<L at time zero, subtracting the steady profile gives theta(x,0)=-100*x/L K. Its sine-series coefficient is b_j=(2/L)*integral(theta(x,0)*sin(j*pi*x/L),x=0..L)=200*(-1)^j/(j*pi) K. In particular the first coefficient is -200/pi K and its decay rate is pi^2/100 s^(-1).
For the three-interior-point method of lines, the first discrete decay rate is (alpha/h^2)*(2-sqrt(2))=(4/25)*(2-sqrt(2)) s^(-1), approximately 0.0937258300203 s^(-1) to twelve significant digits. This differs from the continuum rate 0.0986960440109 s^(-1). The difference follows from the different spatial operators and belongs to the discretisation claim, separately from the arithmetic and verification ledger. Time discretisation, if introduced, adds a further separately stated claim.
variants.name: transient-uniform-interior

problem.instance: The primary is at the origin. The test body starts at (rp,0), with velocity (0,sqrt(mu*(1+e)/rp)). The exact primary mass is chosen so that the nominal mu is 1 m^3/s^2. The periapsis radius is 2/5 m and eccentricity is 3/5.
problem.model:
A test body moves in the Newtonian inverse-square field of a fixed primary, with gravitational parameter mu=G*M. The test-body limit neglects the primary's recoil. Periapsis radius rp and eccentricity e specify the orbit geometry. The initial speed is derived as sqrt(mu*(1+e)/rp), so changing G changes that speed coherently while keeping the geometric ellipse fixed. The speed is not an independently exact measured input.
The reported exact values are nominal mathematical values at the stated central G. G carries a probabilistic standard uncertainty, so these nominal exact values do not assert deterministic enclosure of the physical orbit.
problem.title: Kepler two-body orbit

An integration experiment records observable budgets, time-stepping error and arithmetic contributions separately, and reports measured long-run drift against these constants. True anomaly is a geometric angle and is not assumed proportional to elapsed time. The probabilistic uncertainty in G does not provide the deterministic input enclosure required for a strict physical-value certificate.

observables.derivation:
At the nominal inputs, each length derivative is pi^2, each period derivative is -(621/625)*pi^2 per second, the shared ruler derivative is pi^2, and the shared rate derivative is -2*(621/625)*pi^2. Use w=pi^2/25000 m/s^2 as a common propagated scale. The independent length contributions are 40*w,25*w,20*w; the three independent timing contributions have magnitude 10*w each. The shared ruler contribution is 18*w to every estimate, and the shared stopwatch contribution is -24*w to every estimate.
Consequently Cov(g_i,g_j)=900*w^2 for i!=j, and the diagonal entries are 2600*w^2,1625*w^2,1400*w^2. Equivalently, the full covariance matrix is w^2*[[2600,900,900],[900,1625,900],[900,900,1400]]. The variance of the mean is (2600+1625+1400+6*900)*w^2/9=1225*w^2. Its standard uncertainty is 35*w=7*pi^2/5000=0.0138174461615251... m/s^2. The covariance formula is a linear probabilistic estimate, not a deterministic certificate.

observables.second_route: Group contributions by independent source before forming output covariances. The six individual contributions give mean variance (40^2+25^2+20^2+3*10^2)*w^2/9=325*w^2. The two shared contributions give (18^2+24^2)*w^2=900*w^2. Their sum is again 1225*w^2.

observables.derivation: Treating the three estimates as independent drops the six off-diagonal covariance terms. The resulting mean variance is (2600+1625+1400)*w^2/9=625*w^2, so its standard uncertainty is 25*w=pi^2/1000. This is a comparison calculation that contradicts the declared shared sources.

problem.instance: Three nominally identical pendulums each have measured length 621/625 m and period 2 s. They have different independent length-reading uncertainties and identical independent timing uncertainties. Their shared ruler offset and stopwatch rate have nominal value zero. The exact defined standard acceleration 9.80665 m/s^2 is supplied only for comparison.
problem.model:
The small-angle simple-pendulum model gives g_i=4*pi^2*L_i/T_i^2. The measurement equations are L_i=l_i+ruler_offset and T_i=t_i*(1+stopwatch_rate). Each measured l_i and t_i has its own independent standard uncertainty. The common ruler offset and stopwatch rate are shared random inputs, independent of one another and of the six independent readings. First-order propagation retains their induced cross-covariances.
Uncertainty mode zero uses the standard-uncertainty records. Mode one instead uses the corresponding records ending in _enclosed. Each pair describes alternative declarations of the same measurement or instrument source and is never composed as two inputs. The enclosure records impose additional deterministic assumptions; their half-widths are not confidence limits inferred from the standard uncertainties and supply no variances.
problem.title: Gravitational acceleration from pendulum periods

variants.description: replace the probabilistic declarations by separately assumed deterministic bounds on every relevant input
variants.expected:
Use the eight _enclosed records in the same measurement equations. All lengths and periods stay positive throughout their enclosures. Each gravity estimate increases with its length and the shared ruler offset, and decreases with its measured period and the shared stopwatch rate. Therefore simultaneous endpoint choices attain the exact extrema of the unweighted mean.
The average independent length half-width is (0.0016+0.001+0.0008)/3=17/15000 m. Adding the shared ruler half-width gives 139/75000 m. Thus the upper and lower mean length numerators are 74659/75000 m and 74381/75000 m. The measured period endpoints are 4967/2484 s and 4969/2484 s, and the shared rate factors are 2069/2070 and 2071/2070.
The exact mean enclosure is [g_lower,g_upper], where g_lower=4*pi^2*(74381/75000)*(2484/4969)^2*(2070/2071)^2 and g_upper=4*pi^2*(74659/75000)*(2484/4967)^2*(2070/2069)^2, both in m/s^2. A radius about the nominal mean g0=(621/625)*pi^2 is max(g0-g_lower,g_upper-g0). These nonlinear endpoint expressions include interaction effects and provide a worst-case bound under the declared enclosure assumptions.
The half-widths are independent deterministic declarations, even where their magnitudes equal the standard uncertainties in the other mode. An enclosure supplies no variance. Conversely, the standard uncertainties alone do not provide this deterministic bound.
variants.name: deterministic-instrument-and-reading-enclosures

observables.derivation:
The ladder MNA system is [[G,B],[B^T,D]]*[v,iV]^T=[j,e]^T, with G=[[1,-1,0,0],[-1,3,-1,0],[0,-1,3,-1],[0,0,-1,2]] S, B=[1,0,0,0]^T, D=[0] ohm, j=[0,0,0,0]^T A and e=[Vs] V. G has shape 4 by 4, B has shape 4 by 1, B^T has shape 1 by 4 and D has shape 1 by 1. The voltage vector has four entries in V and iV has one entry in A.
The current equations require [G]=A/V=S and [B]=A/A=1. The voltage equation requires [B^T]=V/V=1 and [D]=V/A=ohm, including when D is zero. This is the quotient-dimension check; the concatenated unknown vector has no single physical dimension. The final equation is v0=Vs=1 V.
observables.description: ladder source-node voltage

problem.model:
The dimensionless Hilbert matrix is H_n[i,j]=1/(i+j-1), with indices starting at one. It is symmetric positive definite. The exact right-hand side is b_i=sum from j=1 to n of 1/(i+j-1), so the exact solution is the all-ones vector. The six entry observables and six inverse-entry observables below specify the upper triangles at order three; symmetry specifies their lower triangles.
Certification uses binary64, round to nearest even, no fused multiply-add, LU with partial pivoting and no recovery. Exactly representable matrix and right-hand-side entries import without a representation radius; entries binary64 cannot represent receive a half-ulp enclosure. A validated bound q on norm_2(I-Z*A), for an approximate inverse Z, gives g=norm_2(Z)/(1-q) if q<1. With residual bound rho, input bounds rA and rB, and candidate norm bound xnorm, the certified radius is R=g*(rho+rB+rA*xnorm)/(1-g*rA) if g*rA<1. Success requires R/norm_2(xhat)<=relative_budget; otherwise the requested guarantee is refused. Conditioning estimates below predict outcomes and do not replace these checks.

observables.derivation:
For v=[24,15,25]^T, exact multiplication gives K*v=[0,0,16]^T. The Rayleigh quotient for K^T*K is 16^2/(24^2+15^2+25^2)=256/1426=128/713. The smallest eigenvalue cannot exceed this quotient. Thus sigma_min(K)<=sqrt(128/713)<1/2, while every unpivoted QR diagonal is at least 16/25>1/2. A diagonal-only rank diagnostic at the stated threshold misses the small singular value.
For general n, U^(-1)[i,j]=c*(1+c)^(j-i-1) for i<j, with unit diagonal. The last inverse column therefore gives sigma_min(K_n)<=s^(n-1)/sqrt(1+c^2*sum((1+c)^(2*j),j=0..n-2)). Keeping just its first entry gives the simpler bound sigma_min(K_n)<=16/(3*2^n). This exposes the growing separation from the trailing QR diagonal s^(n-1). Every finite matrix remains exactly nonsingular.

problem.instance:
At order three, K=[[1,-3/5,-3/5],[0,4/5,-12/25],[0,0,16/25]], with right-hand side [-1/5,8/25,16/25]^T. Its inverse is [[1,3/4,3/2],[0,5/4,15/16],[0,0,25/16]].
At order three, W=[[1,0,1],[-1,1,1],[-1,-1,1]], with right-hand side [2,1,-1]^T. For general order, the Wilkinson right-hand side is b_i=3-i for i<n and b_n=2-n.
problem.model:
The Kahan matrix is K_n=D*U, where D=diag(1,s,...,s^(n-1)), U has unit diagonal, entries -c above the diagonal and zero entries below it, and c^2+s^2=1. The fixed angle has c=3/5 and s=4/5. Every column has Euclidean norm one, while an unpivoted QR factorisation has Q=I and R=K_n.
The Wilkinson construction here is the Gaussian-elimination partial-pivoting growth matrix: diagonal entries are one, entries below the diagonal are minus one, the last column is all ones, and remaining entries are zero. Equal-magnitude pivot candidates are resolved by choosing the smallest row index, so elimination makes no row swaps. This is the growth construction, rather than the symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue example, because the fixture stresses elimination growth and factorisation choices.
For both matrices the exact right-hand side is the matrix times the all-ones vector. Certification uses binary64, round to nearest even, no fused multiply-add, LU with partial pivoting, exact import for binary64-representable entries and half-ulp enclosures only for inexact imports, and no recovery. With q>=norm_2(I-Z*A), use g=norm_2(Z)/(1-q) only if q<1. With validated rho,rA,rB,xnorm, use R=g*(rho+rB+rA*xnorm)/(1-g*rA) only if g*rA<1. Success requires R/norm_2(xhat)<=relative_budget. All outcome predictions remain expectations to be confirmed or corrected by the feasibility bite.
problem.title: Kahan and Wilkinson matrices

The exact growth factor is 2^53=9007199254740992. Nevertheless, the all-ones candidate is exactly recovered by the specified elimination: the transformed right-hand side is 1+2^(i-1) for i<n and 2^(n-1) in the last row. At n=54 these integers are representable in binary64, and back substitution gives every component exactly one.
The inverse has last row entries 2^(-j) for j<n and 2^(-(n-1)) for j=n. For i<n, its row has zeros before column i, entry 1/2 in column i, entries -2^(i-j-1) for i<j<n, and entry -2^(i-n) in the last column. Every absolute row sum and column sum is one. Thus norm_2(W^(-1))<=1 and norm_2(W)<=n, giving kappa_2(W)<=54 and a conditioning estimate kappa*u below 6e-15.
Success under the stated certificate and relative budget 1e-6 is expected. The inverse entries are dyadic, and the independent residual of the exact candidate is zero. Conversion and verification bounds still have to be recorded. The large elimination growth alone is not grounds for refusal.

variants.description: the transformed right-hand side loses a unit in binary64
variants.expected:
The exact solution is fifty-five ones and the exact growth factor is 2^54=18014398509481984. At elimination stage 53, the transformed entry in row 54 becomes 2^53+1, which rounds to 2^53 under ties-to-even. The last-row entry at that stage is 2^53-1; adding the rounded row-54 entry produces 2^54-1, which rounds to 2^54. Back substitution therefore gives xhat_54=0 and every other component one.
The exact represented-center residual is b-W*xhat=W*e_54, with entries 1 and -1 in rows 54 and 55 and zeros elsewhere. Its norm is sqrt(2), and the actual candidate error has norm one. Any honest enclosing radius is therefore at least one, far above the relative budget 1e-6 for a candidate norm sqrt(54). Refusal is required for this candidate even though kappa_2(W)<=55 and kappa*u is only about 6e-15. This distinguishes a poor candidate caused by growth and rounding from ill-conditioning of the underlying problem.

observables.derivation:
Set t=b^2 and u=a^2. Direct integer squaring gives t=1095345216 and u=6024398689. Since (11/2)*t=6024398688, the exact relation is u=(11/2)*t+1.
The polynomial part is P=(1335/4)*t^3+11*u^2*t-u*t^3-121*u*t^2-2*u+(11/2)*t^4. Substituting u=(11/2)*t+1 gives 11*u^2*t=(1331/4)*t^3+121*t^2+11*t, -u*t^3=-(11/2)*t^4-t^3, -121*u*t^2=-(1331/2)*t^3-121*t^2, and -2*u=-11*t-2. Fourth-, second- and first-degree terms cancel pairwise. The cubic coefficient is (1335+1331-4-2662)/4=0. Therefore P=-2 exactly.
